RFC 6265 §4.1.1: "The semantics of the cookie-value are not defined by this document. ... servers that wish to store arbitrary data in a cookie-value SHOULD encode that data". ASP.NET Core cookie auth: "To create a cookie holding user information, construct a ClaimsPrincipal. The user information is serialized and stored in the cookie." — a self-contained value in a cookie with no server record.

app-state.md: "The in-memory cache provider stores session data in the memory of the server where the app resides. In a server farm scenario: Use sticky sessions to tie each session to a specific app instance ... A better approach is to use a Redis, SQL Server, or Azure Postgres distributed cache". distributed.md: distributed cached data "Survives server restarts". So restart loss is supported by implication; 'a shared store is needed' is too strong — sticky sessions are a documented alternative. Also mis-kinded: this is behavior, not opinion.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Sessions kept in one API process's memory are lost when that process restarts, so clients must log in again. When more than one copy runs, either every copy must reach a shared session store, or each client must always be sent to the copy holding its session.

issues.text: Overstated: a shared session store is not the only option with several copies; ASP.NET Core docs list sticky sessions (each session tied to one instance) as an alternative. Same overstatement is claim 8 (verdict rephrased).
issues.quote: A session store grows with every logged-in client and has to be reachable from every copy of the API that answers requests.
issues.fix: Replace with: "A session store grows with every logged-in client, and every copy of the API that might receive a client's request has to reach that client's record." Update claim 8 text to the suggested_text in its verdict and set its kind to behavior, needs_verification true.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: general statement that a token stays valid until it expires. Not true for token-based login in general (a server can add a check that rejects a token early, and changing the key it checks against rejects every token); only true of this app's code. Not in the claims ledger; §6 repeats it ("a token keeps working until it expires").
issues.quote: because the server keeps nothing, it also has nothing to delete: a token stays valid until it expires, even if you would like to end that login sooner.
issues.fix: §4: "...it also has nothing to delete: ending one token before it expires needs something extra on the server, which is exactly the store tokens were avoiding." §6: "...while a token keeps working until it expires unless the server adds something to check it against." Add a claim (kind behavior, section 4/6) for the softened wording; do not detail revocation (depth_notes).

issues.text: Unlisted claim and conditional recommendation not in ledger: sessions can be ended at once by deleting the record, and sessions are 'the simpler fit' under a condition. Both are challengeable (behavior + opinion) and must be ledgered.
issues.quote: a session can be ended at once by deleting its record, while a token keeps working until it expires. When ending a login immediately matters more than avoiding a store, sessions are the simpler fit.
issues.fix: Add two claims to .meta.json: (a) kind behavior, section 6, 'deleting a session record makes the next request with that id find nothing'; (b) kind opinion, section 6, the 'simpler fit' sentence with its condition. Keep text; apply the §6 softening from the §4 issue.

issues.quote: Nothing on the server can end it early; it keeps working until it expires, about seven hours from now.
issues.fix: Option a en: "No code in this app can end that one token early; it keeps working until it expires, about seven hours from now." vi: "Không có code nào trong app này kết thúc riêng token đó sớm được; nó vẫn dùng được cho tới khi hết hạn, khoảng bảy giờ nữa." issues.text: Claim 8 is ledgered as kind opinion with needs_verification false, but 'a restart loses in-memory sessions' is a behavior statement; behavior claims cannot skip verification.
issues.quote: Most likely `401`. A session record kept in the API's memory disappears when the process restarts
issues.fix: In .meta.json set claim 8 kind to behavior, needs_verification true, source_hint refs app-state.md (in-memory provider) and distributed.md ('Survives server restarts'). Lesson text can stay.
